text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
-- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said the government would continue to spend privatisation revenues on reducing state debt.
-- Domestic drug producers do not cut prices despite the abolition of Hungary's customs surcharge today.
-- The Finance Ministry will pay out the first instalment of a guarantee, worth 5.5 billion forints, on Postabank's risky assets.
-- A Hungarian teacher in Roznava, Slovakia was sacked for breaching new regulations prohibiting the issue of school certificates in the Hungarian language.
-- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny told the parliament that nobody would be operated in hospitals, financed by the social security, sooner than others for paying more.
